questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four documented paths for migrating a Hive metastore table to Unity Catalog?
options: Upgrade wizard + SYNC
CLONE
CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT (CTAS)
DELETE FROM hive_metastore and manually re-upload the files
questions.explain: The four real paths are the upgrade wizard/SYNC, CLONE, CTAS, and UCX for workspace-scale automation — manually deleting and re-uploading isn't a documented migration path.

questions.q: What does adding DRY RUN to a SYNC statement do?
options: Permanently deletes the source Hive table after syncing
Reports what the sync would do without making any actual change
Runs the sync only on weekdays
Converts a managed table into an external table immediately
questions.explain: DRY RUN is SYNC's preview mode — it reports the outcome without touching the source table or creating the destination table.

questions.q: What happens in a notebook when someone queries a table through its old hive_metastore path after that table has been migrated?
options: The query silently fails with no explanation
Databricks shows a strikethrough and a deprecation tooltip, with a Quick Fix option to update the reference
The notebook automatically deletes the old query
Nothing — Databricks has no way to detect this
questions.explain: Once a table has an upgraded Unity Catalog equivalent, Databricks flags the old hive_metastore reference inline with a strikethrough, an explanatory tooltip, and a Quick Fix that can rewrite the query to the new path.

options: A Unity Catalog privilege type
A Databricks Labs toolkit that automates assessment and migration across an entire workspace
The SQL function used to grant access to a share
A replacement for the SYNC command
questions.explain: UCX is a Databricks Labs open-source toolkit that sequences assessment, group migration, table mapping, and table migration as coordinated jobs across an entire workspace, rather than one table at a time.

questions.q: What happens to the original Hive table after running SYNC TABLE to upgrade it to Unity Catalog?
options: It is immediately and permanently deleted
It is left untouched, and SYNC can be re-run later to pick up changes
It is converted into a Delta Share automatically
It becomes read-only for all users
questions.explain: SYNC is non-destructive — it leaves the original Hive table in place and can be re-run on a schedule to pick up new or changed tables in the source schema.
